purpose: A curated knowledge base for working with TYPO3, for the three audiences that do: the core contributor, the extension author, and the site developer. It holds the conventions each subsystem is built on and how its mechanisms are used, the core's own contribution process — the rules, the Gerrit workflow, the scripts and test suites — and a catalog of the registered backend UI components. It also answers what is registered in the installation it was started in, which no bundled snapshot could get right. Every answer says which TYPO3 versions it holds for and which of the three kinds of work it belongs to.
instructions: A conventions catalog for working with TYPO3 — the core contribution process included — not a patch assistant. Almost everything here comes from this server's own bundled knowledge: it does not read your working tree, so it does not know your changed files, which tests cover them, or whether a path or identifier still exists on your branch — discover that in the checkout yourself, then bring the concrete paths back to typo3_architecture_lookup and typo3_task_guide. The exception is what no bundled answer could get right, because it is a property of an installation rather than of TYPO3: which icons are registered, which labels exist, which backend modules there are, and what a configuration value actually is at runtime. Those are asked of the TYPO3 installation this server was started in, through its own console — or read from the files its packages ship where there is no command or no reachable console, which every answer says of itself. The knowledge is bound to versions: it covers several TYPO3 lines, a statement that does not hold on all of them carries the range it does hold on, and answers are filtered by targetVersion or by the version of the installation being read. Call typo3_server_scope for what is covered, at which depth, which tool answers what, which versions, and which installation — if any — is being read.

covers.depth: Curated prose. The rules a patch is judged by, not a full style guide.

covers.topic: Gerrit workflow: setup, pushing, amending, backports
covers.depth: Curated prose, command level. Covers the local git side; it cannot talk to the Gerrit server.

Rules plus a working draft and check, including 72-character body wrapping. The subject and body conventions are also served without the core workflow, for a commit in a repository that has no Forge issue and no release branches: workflow="project".

covers.topic: runTests.sh suites, options, and targeted invocation
covers.depth: Every suite this knowledge base knows, with the command, the targeted form, and when to use it. The script is part of the core repository, so paths that read as a project or third-party extension get the boundary stated instead of a command.

covers.topic: Core architecture conventions: DI, events and hooks, TCA and FormEngine, FormEngine data providers, DataHandler, routing, Fluid templates and ViewHelpers, frontend page rendering with PAGEVIEW, how a sitepackage is laid out, TypoScript site sets and TSconfig, language files, upgrade wizards, frontend DataProcessors, upgrading an installation, testing strategy
covers.depth: Conventions per subsystem, matched by path or topic, from both angles: what a change to the subsystem has to satisfy, and how the mechanism is used. It describes how the core is built, never what your checkout contains.

covers.topic: Backend CSS architecture, design tokens, class naming
covers.depth: Curated prose covering the Sass sources, the token contract, and the component structure.

covers.topic: Backend UI components: markup, variants, custom properties
covers.depth: Hand-curated subset of the backend components, not every CSS class in the core. Each entry carries the TYPO3 majors it was verified on; with targetVersion, one that was not verified there is withheld with what to check instead of handed over.

covers.topic: Translation domains: how the domain of an XLF file is derived
covers.depth: Complete and computed, not a snapshot: the core's own path-to-domain rules ported here — the class that holds them is TranslationDomainMapper on one branch and TranslationDomainResolver on the next, so compare against whichever your checkout has, so any XLF path in any extension resolves — including a file that does not exist yet. Where the installation being read is older than translation domains, the full LLL:EXT: reference is the answer instead: the domain form renders nothing there.

The core revision, branch, and verification date behind every catalog answer, contrasted with the TYPO3 version of the installation being read, and how many entries were verified on a stated target version.

covers.topic: What is registered in the installation you are working in: labels, icons, backend modules, Fluid namespaces, effective configuration
covers.depth: Answered by that installation rather than from a snapshot, across the packages it has active — project extensions included. Its console does the answering wherever a command exists; the icon registry has none, so it is read from the packages, and the labels and the Fluid namespaces are read from there too when the console cannot be reached. Every answer carries answeredBy, so a weaker source is visible as one. Unavailable when no installation is reachable, and then said so rather than answered empty.

covers.topic: The project around the installation: its extensions, its sites and their sets, its own commands, and what one of those extensions registers
covers.depth: Read from the repository's files — composer.json, package.json, config/sites — so it answers on a fresh clone, before anything is installed or migrated. It describes what is there, and does not judge it. Per extension: the tables its TCA defines and extends, the content elements it adds to tt_content and the Fluid template each renders through, its backend modules and routes, its icons, its site sets, its service tags, its middlewares, its Fluid roots and namespaces, and the shape of its Classes/ directory — declared in files, so what ext_localconf.php does with a PHP call is not in it.

covers.topic: What a TYPO3 version broke, deprecated, added or noted
covers.depth: The changelog the installed core ships, one entry per change, searched by words, type and version. It covers exactly the versions that installation has — a newer one is not in it.

doesNotCover.topic: Your checkout: changed files, branch, working tree, local git state
doesNotCover.why: This server answers from its own bundled knowledge and never reads, inspects, or runs anything against a TYPO3 core checkout. It cannot be pointed at one.
doesNotCover.instead: Determine the changed paths yourself (git status, git diff --name-only), then pass them to typo3_architecture_lookup and typo3_task_guide to get the conventions and checks that apply to them.

doesNotCover.topic: The core source itself: API signatures, TCA of a table, existing implementations
doesNotCover.why: The knowledge base describes conventions, not code. No core sources ship with it.
doesNotCover.instead: Read the checkout. Use this server for how the subsystem is built and what a patch has to satisfy.

doesNotCover.topic: Which test covers a given file
doesNotCover.why: Test coverage is a property of the checkout, and no index of it is bundled.
doesNotCover.instead: Core tests mirror the class path below typo3/sysext/<ext>/Tests/Unit/ and Tests/Functional/, so typo3/sysext/core/Classes/DataHandling/DataHandler.php is covered by typo3/sysext/core/Tests/Unit/DataHandling/DataHandlerTest.php. Look the file up there, then ask typo3_test_run_guide for the targeted runTests.sh invocation.

doesNotCover.topic: Frontend theming: the CSS and the JavaScript a website renders
doesNotCover.why: Everything here about CSS and TypeScript describes the TYPO3 backend interface — its Sass sources, its --typo3-* token contract, its light and dark color schemes, its move away from Bootstrap. For a theme extension those are not a milder version of the right answer, they are the opposite of it. How a theme extension is laid out is a different question and is not excluded here: the core ships its own theme as a system extension, and the conventions it establishes — the template tree, the layout names, the backend layout files — are in the architecture hints.
doesNotCover.instead: typo3_architecture_lookup withholds the Backend CSS and Backend TypeScript hints where a task names the frontend, and returns what does transfer — Fluid, TypoScript, PHP, and the sitepackage layout. The styling itself is documented at https://docs.typo3.org.

doesNotCover.topic: Whether a component or CSS class still exists on your branch
doesNotCover.why: The component catalog is a snapshot of one pinned core revision; a miss means "not in this snapshot", never "does not exist".
doesNotCover.instead: Call typo3_catalog_scope for the revision behind it, and verify against the checkout when you work on a different branch.

doesNotCover.topic: Gerrit server state: review status, patch sets, votes, CI results
doesNotCover.why: The server talks to nothing over the network.
doesNotCover.instead: Use the Gerrit web UI or git. The local side of the workflow — pushing, amending, backporting — is covered by typo3://core/typo3-gerrit-workflow.

doesNotCover.topic: Work outside TYPO3 core contribution: site setup, project or third-party extension development, configuring an installation with TypoScript, upgrading an installation
doesNotCover.why: The knowledge base is scoped to contributing to the core. Shipping TypoScript defaults from a system extension is core work and is covered; writing TypoScript to configure a site is not, and neither is a package under packages/ or an extension outside typo3/sysext/.
doesNotCover.instead: Use the TYPO3 documentation at https://docs.typo3.org/.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Which files the task actually touches
checkoutDiscovery.how: git status --short and git diff --name-only in the core checkout, then call typo3_architecture_lookup with those paths for the conventions that apply to them.
Core tests mirror the class path below typo3/sysext/<ext>/Tests/Unit/ and Tests/Functional/. Find the file there, then ask typo3_test_run_guide for the targeted runTests.sh invocation.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: The branch you are on and the branches the change is meant for
checkoutDiscovery.how: git branch --show-current. In the normal case the patch targets main and the merging core team member handles the backport; push to a release branch only when the bug does not exist on main.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Whether the paths, classes, labels, and identifiers named in an answer still exist on that branch
checkoutDiscovery.how: Grep the checkout. The catalogs are a snapshot of one revision — typo3_catalog_scope names it.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Whether an icon identifier is registered, and which one spells the shape you want
checkoutDiscovery.how: Ask typo3_icon_lookup: it reads the registry of the installation this server was started in, the T3Icons set and every installed package included. Where there is no reachable installation, the same three places can be read by hand — typo3/sysext/core/Resources/Public/Icons/T3Icons/icons.json, the Configuration/Icons.php of each package, and typo3/sysext/core/Resources/Public/Icons/Flags/ for the flags-* family.

checkoutDiscovery.establish: Whether a label for this wording already exists
checkoutDiscovery.how: Ask typo3_label_lookup: it searches the labels of the installation this server was started in, across the packages it has active and with the resource overrides it applies — neither of which a grep can tell you. Where the console cannot be reached it reads the same packages' XLF files instead and says so; only where there is no installation at all is there nothing to ask.

routing.when: Starting a core task and looking for the applicable conventions and checks
About to write backend markup or invent a CSS class name
About to run tests or any other core check
Working in a concrete file and unsure about the subsystem's conventions
Writing or amending the commit message
Pushing for review, amending a patch set, or backporting
A catalog lookup found nothing that should exist
Needing the translation domain an XLF file resolves to
About to write user-facing text or invent a label key
routing.call: typo3_label_lookup with words from the wording

routing.when: About to reference an icon identifier
Needing a configuration value as it really is at runtime, not as the core ships it
Working on a backend module and needing its registration
Unsure which Fluid namespace prefixes a template may use undeclared
About to recommend a command, or asking what this project consists of
Asking what a version changed, or whether an API is still there
Upgrading or maintaining an installation, and needing the order of operations
routing.call: typo3_task_guide, then typo3_project_scope and typo3_changelog_lookup for what this one is and what the target version changed

routing.when: Working in one extension and needing what it registers
